claims.text: Coupling DFT, anharmonic phonon calculations, and explicit electron-phonon coupling can decouple lattice and electronic thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed framework will be roughly twice as accurate as earlier Debye-temperature-based or conflated models.
The framework is applicable to ideal, defect-free bulk crystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
The framework is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed calculations can separately determine phonon scattering rates, phonon lifetimes, and electronic relaxation times.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below approximately 200 K.
The 300–1200 K regime in specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen represents realistic impurity conditions.
Detailed atomic-scale structural data and calculated scattering parameters capture perfect-lattice dynamics.
The framework explicitly captures defect-induced scattering from oxygen impurities.
Explicitly separating lattice and electronic channels avoids oversimplified Debye-temperature approximations.
Including anharmonic and defect scattering through ab initio calculations will improve agreement with temperature-dependent thermal-conductivity experiments.
The combined predicted lattice and electronic conductivities will give total thermal conductivity within a factor of two of experiment.
The model will reproduce the comparable magnitudes of lattice and electronic contributions below approximately 200 K.
The model will match total thermal conductivity over 300–1200 K.
Earlier models conflated lattice and electronic contributions while representing ideal, defect-free crystals.
The framework should remain reliable for bulk crystalline HfNbTaTiZr containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
Accuracy may diminish above 1 wt.% oxygen or in non-bulk geometries and alternative processing conditions.
Uncertainty in electron-phonon interactions and defect scattering makes the precise quantitative accuracy gain uncertain.
